title_he: עוֹד מְעַט יִתָּקַע הַשּׁוֹפָר וִירִיעַ צְבָא שָׁמַיִם
review: 2:1–2 יִתָּקַע שׁוֹפָר … וְיָרִיעַ צְבָא שָׁמַיִם — the Arabic يَدْوِي بُوقٌ وَيَهْتِفُ جُنْدُ السَّمَاء is 1 Thess 4:16 (יְהוָה … בְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר) with 1 Cor 15:52; תָּקַע is the blowing verb of the shofar and רִיעַ the shout, so the two sounds of the verse stay two verbs.

2:4 עֲלוּ לִקְרָאתוֹ בָּאֲוִיר — the Arabic اصْعَدُوا إِلَى الْهَوَاء is 'ascend into the air' (1 Thess 4:17, בָּאֲוִיר); the Hebrew keeps the ascent imperative addressed to the saints, since the print puts it in quotation marks as the archangel's cry and not as a description.

3:2 אֲרוּחַת חֲתֻנַּת הַשֶּׂה — the Arabic عَشَاءُ عُرْسٍ لِلْخَرُوف is Rev 19:9 (אֲרוּחַת חֲתֻנַּת הַשֶּׂה) quoted almost verbatim; חֲתֻנָּה is the glossary's fixed wedding noun, and שֶׂה is kept for the Lamb rather than כֶּבֶשׂ, since the Apocalypse's phrase is the one being cited.

3:3–4 רְבָבוֹת … וַאֲלָפִים — the Arabic رَبَوَاتٌ … وَالْأُلُوف is the myriads-and-thousands of Dan 7:10 (רִבְּוָן … וְאַלְפִין) and Rev 5:11; the two numbers are kept as two, since the Arabic distinguishes them and the verse's force is innumerability.

4:4 וְעַד לְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים — the Arabic إِلَى آبَادِ الْآبِدِين is the Hebrew idiom's own shape (Ps 145:13, מַלְכוּתְךָ … בְּכָל־דֹּר וָדֹר); the doubled עוֹלָם is used because 'to the ages of ages' is a Hebrew construction before it is a Greek one.
